critic.scope: PCW.md, all 851 cards (keyword sweeps over every card plus its harvest item), work/gaps.jsonl (48 lines), pcw.py dupes, every platform limit (289 rows: field, number, confidence, checked date), trend evidence dates and compliance as_of dates, and 43 cards read in full: 30 from a seeded random sample (random.Random(20261013), 3 per kind across all 10 kinds) plus 13 deliberate picks (plat:instagram_reel, plat:instagram_hashtags, plat:x_long_post, plat:sms_india_dlt, comp:dpdp_act_rules, comp:it_rules_sgi_2026, comp:asci_ai_sgc_labelling, trend:chatgpt_ads, lang:hinglish_roman, tone:sarkari_formal, edit:ai_tell_removal, tech:awareness_level_matching, genre:interview_qa). hook:testimonial came up in both.
critic.inventory: 851 harvest items, 851 cards (genre 290, technique 127, platform 103, compliance 79, framework 67, hook 54, editing 45, tone 35, trend 30, language 21), validate 0 issues. Genre, hook and framework cards: 411/411 judged, pass 409, weak 1, wrong 0, not_tested 1. The other 440 cards are validated against their cited sources only.
critic.method: Gaps are things a professional Indian and global content writer is likely to be asked for in 2026 that no card covers (zero or passing keyword hits). Weak cards are cards whose own text is contradicted, under-sourced or untested. Doubts are limits on what the verification actually proves.

gaps: Indian commerce surfaces with no platform card: Meesho, Myntra and Nykaa seller listings (named only inside genre:marketplace_listing and genre:product_description), quick-commerce listings (Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart), B2B listings (IndiaMART and ONDC: zero hits), Justdial (named in genre cards only), property portals (99acres, MagicBricks, Housing.com: zero hits) and OTA hotel listings beyond plat:airbnb_listing.

News distribution surfaces: zero hits for Google Discover, Google News, Web Stories, 60-word news apps (Inshorts style) and Dailyhunt. genre:news_story, genre:live_blog and genre:news_explainer have no card for the headline, image and description rules of the surfaces that carry them.

Indian news-media rules: no compliance card for the Press Council of India Norms of Journalistic Conduct (one passing mention), the NBDSA code (zero hits) or the Digital Media Ethics Code in Part III of the IT Rules 2021 for digital news publishers (named only in the title of comp:it_rules_sgi_2026). Scripts have nothing on CBFC certification (zero hits).

Indian sector ad codes not harvested: Drugs and Cosmetics Act and Rules for cosmetic and Ayush claims (zero hits for the Act), AMFI / SEBI mutual-fund advertisement rules and SEBI investment-adviser and research-analyst ad rules (zero hits; comp:sebi_finfluencer_association covers only the association ban), COTPA tobacco and surrogate advertising (passing mentions only), the Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act 1986 (zero hits), and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020 listing disclosures such as seller details and country of origin (zero hits).

Global consumer and privacy law not harvested: the EU Unfair Commercial Practices Directive and the Price Indication Directive's prior-price rule for discount copy, California CCPA/CPRA and other US state privacy laws, the UK Online Safety Act and the ICO Children's code, and prize-promotion / sweepstakes rules (US states; India's Prize Competition Act 1955). All zero hits.
Accessibility law outside India: the European Accessibility Act (applies from 28 June 2025) and the ADA have zero hits; only WCAG 2.2, GIGW 3.0 and the RPwD Act are carded.

Platform policies a writer hits daily: no card for the WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy (opt-in, template categories), Apple App Store Review Guidelines on accurate metadata, or the Google Play metadata policy, although genre:app_store_listing, plat:apple_app_store and plat:google_play_listing exist.

Genres with no card (zero keyword hits): sponsored newsletter placement (newsletter ad), event or creator sponsorship proposal, assessment items and MCQs for ed-tech, online course landing page or course description, product recall and safety notice, Indian newspaper public notice, open letter and letter to the editor.

Deliverables covered only by language cards: a subtitle file (SRT) as its own deliverable and a narration-only voice-over script (lang:english_subtitles, lang:hindi_subtitles and the video-script genres carry the rules; no genre card has a goal, structure or lint for them).

Platform rows missing on existing cards: plat:tiktok_video records only the Content Posting API caption (2,200 UTF-16 units), not the in-app caption length; plat:threads_post has the 500-character post but nothing on longer text attachments, if Threads offers them; no cards for Instagram or YouTube Live, Instagram broadcast channels, Meta's business AI agents, or ChatGPT ad formats (trend:chatgpt_ads covers the trend, not the surface).

Still no official figure found: Facebook organic Page and group post length, Threads bio, Quora answer, Instagram name and broadcast channel, Moj / Josh / ShareChat limits, email preview text (no inbox provider publishes one; held as a note on plat:email_subject_line, no plat:email_preheader card) and the TikTok bio (low confidence, Wayback copy).

Law that lives only inside a genre card, with no compliance card of its own: RTI Act 2005 (genre:rti_application), ICSI SS-1 (genre:meeting_minutes), POSH Act and the labour codes (genre:policy_document, comp:india_job_ad_non_discrimination), CDSCO / NDCT Rules and ICH E3 (genre:medical_regulatory_writing), EU ePrivacy Directive Art. 13 (inside comp:gdpr_marketing_consent and comp:uk_pecr), and client NDA / portfolio-permission norms (genre:portfolio_case_writeup).

Editing: no card for an Indian newsroom house style (Indian English) and no single readability umbrella (the four score cards are linked instead). The 2026-10-05 gap fix 'add the CSMOP source to edit:cliche_pass' was not applied.

Near-duplicates kept as separate, cross-linked cards (decide if usage shows confusion): pcw.py dupes reports fw:bluf ~ fw:minto_pyramid, genre:recruitment_ad ~ genre:job_description, genre:sales_deck ~ genre:investor_pitch_deck, genre:statement_of_purpose ~ genre:college_essay; the gap log adds affiliate_review / product_review_article, byline_article / thought_leadership_article / opinion_column, brand_story / about_page, editorial_newsletter / creator_newsletter, pillar_page / ultimate_guide, newsjacking_post / topical_ad, podcast_ad_read / sponsored_integration_script, obituary / obituary_notice, fw:oreo / fw:prep, tech:awareness_level_matching / fw:schwartz_awareness_levels.
weak_cards: genre:interview_qa (weak 7 after three rounds): the card's structure, ordering, hard question, Hinglish and fair-reporting guidance held, but its answer length (40-200 words) is unproven because the exemplar_brief supplies about 210 words of transcript for 10-12 exchanges. Fix the test, not the card: give the brief 600-900 words of transcript (or cut the target to 600-800 words), then one re-judge.
hook:testimonial (not_tested): no customer quote was supplied, so the writer correctly slotted every quote. Re-test with a quote the brief supplies and labels as hypothetical.

plat:meta_ads: its row 'hashtags, Instagram feed (maximum) 30' contradicts plat:instagram_hashtags (5 per post, Instagram Help Center) and the avoid line in plat:instagram_reel. Check whether ads have their own cap; otherwise drop the row or point it at plat:instagram_hashtags.

plat:telegram_ads: confidence is high, but the 160-character rule and its quote come from a search summary because promote.telegram.org refused a direct fetch, so the quote may be paraphrase. Re-read the page in a browser or lower the confidence to medium.

plat:x_long_post: confidence is high, but About X Premium refused a fetch on 2026-10-05, and X's own pages disagree (25,000 versus 4,000). The card handles this well (it writes to 4,000); the confidence label overstates it.

comp:rbi_fair_practices_recovery (medium): the rules a collection script depends on most (8 a.m. to 7 p.m. calls, no social-media messages) come from a web-search summary, because the 2025 Directions PDF is behind a CAPTCHA. The card says so; read the PDF before the next refresh.
fw:bencivenga_persuasion_equation (low): sourced to a conversion blog and a post on X; the attribution to Gary Bencivenga is unverified.
lang:gulf_nri_english (low): only the audience size (MEA table) is sourced; every writing rule is marked house practice.
doubtful: Seven of the ten kinds were never sample-tested: 440 cards (technique 127, platform 103, compliance 79, editing 45, tone 35, trend 30, language 21) passed the contract checks and were written from cited sources, but no test piece depended on them and no judge scored whether following them works. Platform numbers were source-checked at harvest: 289 limit rows, 250 high, 24 medium and 15 low confidence.

76 passing cards (66 genre, 7 hook, 3 framework) had a CARD FIX applied after their pass verdict (fix rounds of 2026-10-07) and still say 're-judge pending'. Their verdicts score the card as it was before the fix. Most fixes enriched the exemplar_brief only (about 51), which is low risk; about 9 changed lint rules and 5 changed structure, and those changes are unverified.

Each sample had one LLM judge, and agreement between judges was never measured. No human editor reviewed any sample, and no native Hindi speaker reviewed the Hindi and Hinglish pieces, which only an LLM judge read.
Exemplar briefs are India-first by contract, so the US, UK and global use of most genre cards was exercised less than the Indian use.

Volatile platform limits, each read only once (2026-10-04/05), to re-check first: Instagram hashtags (5, changed in Dec 2025), Instagram Reels length (20 minutes in the app versus 15 through the API), Instagram carousel (20 in the app versus 10 through the API), YouTube Shorts (180 s), X long posts (25,000 versus 4,000), LinkedIn job description (10,000 versus 25,000), Amazon backend search terms (200 versus 249 bytes, forum only) and the Amazon title cap (200).

22 cards rest partly on second-hand reading: search-engine summaries, pages that refused a fetch or sat behind a CAPTCHA, Wayback copies, or harvest notes 'not re-fetched' (among them plat:telegram_ads, plat:x_long_post, plat:tiktok_video, plat:tiktok_profile, comp:rbi_fair_practices_recovery, comp:emblems_names_act_1950 and five tone cards). Their quotes may be paraphrase.

Dated compliance that is moving now: ASCI's AI-labelling guidelines (signed 17 Sep 2026, effective about three months after publication), the IT Rules SGI Second Amendment (a March 2026 draft, status unconfirmed), DPDP Rules phases (consent managers about Nov 2026, main duties about May 2027, from a law-firm summary), EU AI Act Art. 50 after the Digital Omnibus proposal, Online Gaming Act 2025 commencement (secondary source) and the Income-tax Act 2025 renumbering of 80G.

Trends close to their half-life: trend:chatgpt_ads (12 months, US-only evidence from Jan-Feb 2026) and trend:llm_readable_content_myths (12 months) need a re-check by early 2027; trend:hashtags_to_keywords' older evidence (2025-07-10) is already more than 12 months old.
Genre value tiers rest on marketplace category counts and salary-site figures read on one day (Fiverr, Upwork, AmbitionBox, BLS). They rank demand roughly; they are not market sizing.
About 20 language cards mark some rules 'house practice, unsourced'. That is honest, but those rules are a writer's convention, not sourced fact.
tool_limits: pcw.py check counts visible characters only when the optional regex module is installed (otherwise code points), and does not implement X's weighted counting (links count 23) or TikTok's UTF-16 count; the platform cards say how to check those by hand.
Limits in seconds, pixels, bytes per keyword box and button or link counts are not lintable; the platform cards say how to check them by hand.
A platform with several fields is enforced one field at a time (--field); multi-part deliverables (message sets, bios, hook lists) are linted part by part.
Readability grades and the AI-tell list are English-only; Hindi and Hinglish drafts need a read-aloud pass.

next_steps.step: Close the two open verdicts: rewrite genre:interview_qa's exemplar_brief with 600-900 words of transcript and re-judge once; re-test hook:testimonial with a brief-supplied, clearly hypothetical customer quote.

Fix the three confidence and consistency faults: resolve plat:meta_ads' 30-hashtag row against plat:instagram_hashtags; re-read the Telegram Ad Platform guidelines and About X Premium in a browser and set confidence from what the pages say; read RBI's 2025 Responsible Business Conduct Directions PDF for comp:rbi_fair_practices_recovery.

Re-judge the passing cards whose lint or structure changed after their verdict (about 14 of the 76 marked 're-judge pending'), with fresh samples; the brief-only fixes can wait for the next full round.

India gap harvest: compliance cards for the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules (cosmetic and Ayush claims), AMFI / SEBI mutual-fund and adviser ad rules, COTPA and surrogate ads, the 1986 Indecent Representation Act, the E-Commerce Rules 2020, the PCI norms, the NBDSA code and IT Rules Part III; platform cards for Meesho, Myntra, Nykaa, quick-commerce, IndiaMART / ONDC, property portals and OTA listings.

Global gap harvest: EU UCPD and the prior-price rule, the European Accessibility Act, CCPA/CPRA, the UK Online Safety Act and Children's code, prize-promotion law, the WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy, Apple's metadata guideline and Google Play's metadata policy; surface cards for Google Discover, Google News and Web Stories.

Genre gap cards, then sample and judge them like the rest: newsletter sponsorship ad, sponsorship proposal, assessment items / MCQs, course landing page, recall and safety notice, public notice, open letter / letter to the editor, SRT deliverable, narration-only VO script.

Test the untested kinds through the genre tests: in the next verify round, each brief names the platform, tone, language and compliance cards the piece must obey, and the judge scores whether the limits were met and the legal checklist passed. That turns source-only cards into exercised ones without a separate wave.

Keep it current: re-check the dated compliance items monthly and the volatile platform limits quarterly (the list in doubtful), bumping as_of and checked; re-read trend evidence when a card passes its half-life.
Grow work/gaps.jsonl from real writing jobs (the pcw skill appends a line whenever no card fits) and decide the near-duplicate pairs from how often writers pick the wrong one.
